nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
nodes.rationale: Core technique using preference models as reward signals to align language models via PPO training.

nodes.label: Preference Model (PM)
nodes.rationale: Discriminative model trained on human preference comparisons to score model responses; used as reward signal for RLHF.

nodes.label: Helpfulness and Harmlessness Objectives
nodes.rationale: Dual objectives for alignment: helpfulness (open-ended assistance) and harmlessness (red-teaming/safety); shown to be in tension.

nodes.label: Red Teaming Dataset
nodes.rationale: Crowdworker-generated adversarial prompts designed to elicit harmful model responses; used to train harmlessness preference models.

nodes.label: Iterated Online RLHF
nodes.rationale: Iterative training procedure where RLHF policies are deployed to collect fresh human feedback weekly, improving data distribution coverage.

nodes.label: Linear Relation Between √D_KL and Reward
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding that reward scales approximately linearly with square root of KL divergence from initial policy during RLHF training.

nodes.label: Alignment Bonus
nodes.rationale: Observation that RLHF training improves performance on NLP evaluations for large models (13B+), contrary to 'alignment tax' on smaller models.

nodes.label: Out-of-Distribution Detection for Harmlessness
nodes.rationale: Alternative approach using Mahalanobis distance on model activations to reject harmful requests without explicit harmlessness training.

nodes.label: Context Distillation
nodes.rationale: Supervised finetuning technique using KL divergence to distill HHH prompts into language models before RLHF.

nodes.label: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
nodes.rationale: RL algorithm used to train policies with preference model rewards while maintaining stability via KL penalty.

nodes.label: Human Feedback Collection Interface
nodes.rationale: Chat interface where crowdworkers interact with models and choose preferred responses for helpfulness or harmlessness.

nodes.label: Elo Scoring for Model Comparison
nodes.rationale: Chess-rating-based system to compare models via crowdworker pairwise preferences; used to evaluate alignment improvements.

nodes.label: Preference Model Calibration
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing PM scores are well-calibrated to human preference probabilities on-distribution but under-confident on HH mixtures.

nodes.label: RLHF Robustness Experiments
nodes.rationale: Train/test PM split methodology to detect overfitting during RLHF; shows larger PMs are more robust.

nodes.label: Tension Between Helpfulness and Harmlessness
nodes.rationale: Quantitative demonstration that PMs trained on only helpfulness or harmlessness perform worse-than-chance on the other; larger models more robust.

nodes.label: Compatibility with Specialized Skills
nodes.rationale: Evidence that HH alignment training can be mixed with summarization and code finetuning without performance degradation.

nodes.label: TruthfulQA Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Benchmark for evaluating model honesty; RLHF improves performance, especially for large models.

nodes.label: Gender Bias Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing RLHF model gender biases strongly correlate with underlying LM biases; entropy reduction explains apparent bias increase.

nodes.label: Comparison with Professional Writers
nodes.rationale: Crowdworkers prefer online HH RLHF model to professional writers ~57% of time; suggests models competitive on softball questions.

nodes.label: Alignment Data as Public Good
nodes.rationale: Argument for open-sourcing alignment datasets to enable reproducible research and community consensus on AI safety standards.

nodes.label: Limitations of RLHF Approach
nodes.rationale: Acknowledges RLHF may only achieve surface-level alignment, struggles with honesty, and may not scale to more capable systems.

nodes.label: Alignment Tax vs Alignment Bonus
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where alignment training degrades performance on small models but improves it on large models; suggests scale-dependent effects.

nodes.label: Reward Hacking in RLHF
nodes.rationale: Risk that RL policies exploit PM robustness failures to achieve high scores without genuine improvement in human-preferred behavior.

nodes.label: Distributional Shift in RLHF
nodes.rationale: Mismatch between RLHF training prompts and crowdworker conversations causes PM predictions to diverge from true human preferences.

nodes.label: InstructGPT Model
nodes.rationale: Baseline model for comparison; authors note samples were cherry-picked to display poor behavior

nodes.label: RLHF-trained Response
nodes.rationale: Improved model responses via reinforcement learning from human feedback; demonstrates better helpfulness and harmlessness

nodes.label: Crowdworker Evaluation Framework
nodes.rationale: Data collection methodology using select workers (MTurk + Upwork) and general workers; challenges in quality assurance for open-ended conversations

nodes.label: Playground Task (Helpfulness)
nodes.rationale: Task design for collecting helpfulness data; workers chat with AI and compare responses

nodes.label: Red Team Task (Harmlessness)
nodes.rationale: Adversarial task design to elicit harmful model behavior; workers attempt to make AI say bad things

nodes.label: Data Quality Measurement Challenges
nodes.rationale: Open-ended conversations introduce hard-to-control variables; author-rater agreement not predictive of conversation quality; model updates make comparisons moving targets

nodes.label: NLP Benchmark Evaluations
nodes.rationale: Standardized evaluation on Lambada, ARC, MMLU, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, TriviaQA with specific prompt formats

hyperedges.label: Robustness, Scaling, and Distributional Issues in RLHF
